title: Power of 2
subtitle: How to Make the Most of Your Partnerships at Work and in Life
author: Rodd Wagner & Gale Muller
note: On the importance of having a counterweight when you're developing something difficult, whether that's a business or a new technology.

title: Handmade
subtitle: A Scientist's Search for Meaning through Making
author: Anna Ploszajski
note: A journey through materials by way of the craft of making them. A materials engineer's job is often translating an idea between the computer and reality, and this book really brings that home.

title: Pluto's Republic
author: Peter Medawar
note: A collection of essays that gave me a real scepticism of systems and bureaucracies: a group of clever people can do stupid things through no individual's fault.

title: Rebel Ideas
subtitle: The Power of Diverse Thinking
author: Matthew Syed
note: Why diversity of thought is critical to solving hard problems.

title: What Money Can't Buy
subtitle: The Moral Limits of Markets
author: Michael Sandel
note: How money can crowd out norms that used to matter more, and why you should be careful when you change the way people see something.

title: Incognito
subtitle: The Secret Lives of the Brain
author: David Eagleman
note: I'm fascinated by how the brain solves problems, and this book taught me that most of our behaviour is driven by the unconscious mind.
